faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Lens Retaining Ring (Metrology) suitable for Optical lens retaining ring for metrology tools?
faq.a: Titanium Lens Retaining Ring (Metrology) uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address metrology operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Lens Retaining Ring (Metrology)?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Lens Retaining Ring (Metrology) is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for optical lens retaining requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Lens Retaining Ring (Metrology) require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. optical lens retaining components require Electropolishing Ra <0.25um + UHP DI cascade rinse with particle count verification per MIL-STD-1246 Class 1 — tailored for optical lens retaining application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.
